module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture about cardinality of Lindelöf spaces

The conjecture asks for a Lindelöf Tychonoff space where all singletons are G_δ sets
and which has cardinality > 𝔠.

This is Problem 1 in https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf

*Reference:*
* [Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology](https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf)
  by A. V. Arhangel’skii

-/

@[expose] public section

open Cardinal

namespace CardinalityLindelof

/--
Is there a Lindelöf Tychonoff space with singletons as Gδ sets with cardinality greater than
the continuum?

Note: the cited paper uses a blanket convention that all spaces are Tychonoff.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem HasGδSingletons.lindelof_card :
    ∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X),
      T35Space X ∧ HasGδSingletons X ∧ LindelofSpace X ∧ 𝔠 < #X := by
  sorry

-- TODO: under additional axioms (consistent with ZFC), such a space exists.

end CardinalityLindelof

reformulations.difference: The displayed Problem 1 asks whether every Lindelöf space with Gδ points has cardinality at most the continuum. Lean instead states the counterexample-existence task explicitly requested in the paragraph immediately following that question.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On p. 38 the source says, “We are still looking for an example in ZFC of a large Lindelöf space X in which every point is a Gδ,” and its blanket convention requires spaces to be Tychonoff. This request is precisely the Lean existential. In /workspace/review/reformulation.lean I proved that this existential is equivalent to the negation of the universal cardinal bound, using ¬(#X ≤ 𝔠) ↔ 𝔠 < #X. I also proved equivalence with an expanded formulation using Hausdorff complete regularity, countable intersections of open sets for singletons, and countable subcovers. Thus the existential follows the source’s explicit counterexample formulation; it is not being identified with the affirmative universal assertion.

sources_consulted: A. V. Arhangel’skii, Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology (2013), especially p. 38, the blanket Tychonoff convention, Problem 1, and its following paragraph: https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
Local Mathlib: Mathlib/Topology/GDelta/Basic.lean, IsGδ and isGδ_iff_eq_iInter_nat.
Local Mathlib: Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Lindelof.lean, IsLindelof, LindelofSpace, and isLindelof_iff_countable_subcover.
Local Mathlib: Mathlib/Topology/Separation/CompletelyRegular.lean and Mathlib/Topology/Separation/Regular.lean, the separation axioms and their implications.
Local Mathlib: Mathlib/SetTheory/Cardinal/Defs.lean, Mathlib/SetTheory/Cardinal/Basic.lean, and Mathlib/SetTheory/Cardinal/Continuum.lean, cardinality, countability bounds, and the continuum.
review.notes: Checked the sole theorem and all definitions it uses. The cited paper explicitly leaves ZFC counterexample existence open while recording consistent counterexamples, so the research-open tag and TODO agree with it. Scratch Lean checks exclude empty, finite, countable, and discrete Lindelöf spaces as accidental witnesses, verify that the other conditions are jointly satisfied by ℝ, and confirm that Type contains types larger than the continuum. The equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies.
